correctness.rationale: The smooth-curve chord expansion has sagitta kappa delta^2/8 and omitted cap area kappa delta^3/12, uniformly along the C3 curve. Rescaling at the sole density zero by h=n^(-1/(alpha+1)) yields PPP intensity c|x|^alpha dx. Empty-subinterval exponential bounds localize the largest gap for alpha>0; cubic-spacing expectation tails scale R^(1-2alpha), summable precisely for alpha>1/2, yielding a joint Poisson functional. Outside the zero, renewal/exponential local-spacing moments give bulk missing-area coefficient 1/2 integral(kappa/f^2). At alpha=1/2 the divergent logarithm gives 2kappa(0)/(3c^2); independent circle substitution with alpha=.5 confirmed 36.74817976924424, and direct sagitta/cap expansions match. Critical variance and de-Poissonization inequalities are justified by local spacing and monotonicity in sample size. The finite stochastic CHECK.py is corroboration only, not a proof of weak convergence. A material priority risk is Hüsler maximum-spacing work but it alone does not provide the area transition.
residual_risks: Stochastic limit requires uniform tail control, not just convergence on bounded PPP windows; provided argument uses explicit summable exponential/cubic tails.
Highly relevant Hüsler 1988 source full text inaccessible, so priority judgement remains provisional.

value.rationale: A naturally motivated deterioration of boundary sampling quality separates worst-case Hausdorff error from integrated area loss. The sharp alpha=1/2 threshold and jointly coupled limiting laws identify which statistic localizes at the zero; the critical coefficient is a meaningful asymptotic invariant beyond ordinary positive-density estimates.
residual_risks: Priority uncertainty about known gap marginal and inaccessible Hüsler full paper; joint area findings remain independently motivated.

final_claim: For a C3 strictly convex positive-curvature planar body with a unique arclength-density zero f(s)~c|s|^alpha, alpha>0, worst Hausdorff deficiency has scale n^(-2/(alpha+1)) and local inhomogeneous-Poisson max-gap limit, whereas missing area changes at alpha=1/2 from deterministic n^-2 to n^-2 log n to a local Poisson cubic-gap sum, jointly with the Hausdorff limit for alpha>1/2.
limitations: Unique isolated power-law zero and C3 strictly convex positive-curvature planar body; not general multiple zeros or flat points.
Weak convergence, in-probability area laws, not explicit elementary CDF; finite random simulations not proofs.
